# Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga Pācittiya 53 (Bi-Vb Pc53)

**ID:** Bi-Vb Pc53

**Collection:** Vinaya

**Title (English, from literature):** Reviling the community

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga Pācittiya 53, entitled *Gaṇaparibhāsana* ("Reviling the community"), belongs to the Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga of the Vinaya Piṭaka. The core rule stipulates that a nun who in anger reviles or intimidates a group of nuns commits an offense entailing expiation (*yā pana bhikkhunī caṇḍīkatā gaṇaṁ paribhāseyya, pācittiyaṁ*) [Hüsken 1997]. There is no corresponding rule in the Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga [Hüsken 1997].

In the origin story, the nun Thullanandā criticizes the community of nuns over legal decisions concerning the suspended nun Caṇḍakālī, sharing thematic and narrative parallels with Bhikkhunī Saṅghādisesa 4 [Hüsken 1997]. Together with the *padabhājanīya* (word commentary), the rule serves fundamentally as a prohibition against criticizing legally valid monastic procedures and decisions, while also broadly forbidding the reviling or snubbing of fellow nuns [Hüsken 1997]. The casuistry specifies that reviling several nuns, a single nun, or an unordained person incurs an offense of wrong conduct (*dukkaṭa*), while exceptions apply if comments occur in the context of canonical recitation or exposition [Hüsken 1997]. English translations include one by Bhikkhu Brahmali.
